sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Immediate Trigger**: Lord Linlithgow's declaration of India as a belligerent state in **World War II** on September 3, 1939, without the consent of the Central Legislative Assembly or provincial ministries.
• **Core Conflict**: The clash between the **Imperialist War Aims** (British) and the **Nationalist Demand** for a clear statement on India's post-war status and immediate democratic rights.
• **Institutional Response**: The **Congress Working Committee (CWC)** demanded a declaration of war aims and how they would apply to India; the British response (Linlithgow's Statement of Oct 17, 1939) was deemed unsatisfactory.
• **Key Metric**: Congress ministries resigned in **8 out of 11 provinces** (Madras, Bombay, Central Provinces, UP, Bihar, Orissa, NWFP, and later Assam).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: CWC demanded 'War Aims' and 'Constituent Assembly' promise.
Prelims: Understanding the 'Why' behind the resignation.
Refusal to be a 'subordinate ally' in an imperial war.
Mains: Shift from 'Office Acceptance' to 'Mass Mobilization'.

items.definition: The British refusal to define war aims, offering only a 'Consultative Committee' for war efforts, which Congress rejected as a 'hollow promise'.
Celebrated by the Muslim League (led by Jinnah) on Dec 22, 1939, to mark the 'relief' from Congress rule, signaling the widening communal divide.

items.title: Strategic Implications
items.content:
• **Political Vacuum**: Resignation led to the imposition of Section 93 (Governor's Rule) in provinces.
• **Shift in Strategy**: Paved the way for the Individual Satyagraha (1940) and the eventual Quit India Movement (1942).

items.title: Communal Polarization
items.content: • **Muslim League's Opportunism**: Jinnah used the resignation to align closer with the British, gaining leverage for the 'Two-Nation Theory' and the 1940 Lahore Resolution.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'W-A-R' (War, Aims, Resignation).
• **Decoded Meaning**: W (World War II declared), A (Aims demanded by Congress), R (Resignation of Ministries).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often asks if Congress resigned because they supported the Axis powers. This is FALSE. Congress was anti-fascist but refused to support the war as a 'subject nation'.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Constitutional Deadlock' to describe the period between 1939 and 1942, highlighting the failure of the August Offer (1940).

keyTakeaways: The resignation was a principled stand against the unilateral inclusion of India in WWII.
It marked the end of the 'Congress in Office' phase (1937-1939) and the return to confrontational politics.
The event provided the Muslim League with a political opening to consolidate its position as the sole representative of Indian Muslims.
